case: One registered predicate is given the NEGATIVE-FIXTURE SENTINEL as its `implementation_status`, which is what every fixture-introduced predicate carries, and which must not trip the F6D-09 tripwire.
why: This is the exclusion itself, held to a case. `r3-lifecycle-status-as-judgment-subject` patches a predicate INTO the registry to exercise the primitive-argument record-type comparison, and that predicate must declare a status; the status it declares says `negative fixture; never part of the contract`. Before r7-contracts-b the F6D-09 tripwire counted distinct statuses across the whole registry and so fired on r3's own scratch tree, refusing r3 for a reason that had nothing to do with what r3 proves -- a wrong_reason leak, and the suite's whole point is that a rejection for the wrong reason is not a rejection. A benign fixture is what keeps the exclusion from silently widening: if someone ever drops the sentinel from the exclusion, this one fails, and the failure names the reason.

patch.value: negative fixture; never part of the contract
